opening.dry: I had almost made it through dinner without wearing it.
opening.direct: I’m okay. Please give me a napkin before anyone grabs my sleeve.

scenarios.title: More than expected
scenarios.setup: Your date orders several small plates, expecting tasting portions. Full-size dishes begin arriving. The table is running out of space.

opening.playful: In my defence, the word “small” did a lot of work on that menu.
opening.dry: I appear to have ordered for a committee.
opening.direct: I misread the portions. We should sort this out before more arrives.

scenarios.follow: Eli can stop the dishes that have not been prepared. There is still plenty on the table, and your date asks what you feel comfortable sharing.

choices.label: Ask Eli to cancel what is still in the kitchen
choices.fact: Eli cancelled the extra dishes still in the kitchen.
choices.line: Thank you. I got carried away; that part is on me.
choices.follow: Eli cancels the dishes still in the kitchen. Your date looks at the plates already here and asks what you would actually like to share.

choices.label: Call it a tasting menu and let your date choose first
choices.fact: The accidental feast became a tasting-menu joke and the date chose a first dish.

line.playful: A tasting menu. Very elegant. Apparently we’re tasting Thursday through Sunday.
line.dry: Excellent branding. It remains a lot of potatoes.
line.direct: All right. First pick is mine, but nobody has to finish this.

choices.follow: Your date picks a favourite dish. The game is funny, but there is still more food than the table needs.

choices.label: Slide your own plate clear of the incoming feast
choices.fact: The player protected their own meal before the table had agreed what to share.

agendas.goal: Enjoy playful chemistry without having to perform all evening.
agendas.hint: A joke can give way to a plain, honest remark.
agendas.understood: Recognizes that enjoying the banter does not mean needing constant entertainment.
agendas.respected: Makes room for an ordinary, sincere exchange rather than demanding another joke.

agendas.goal: Have an evening off from organizing everyone else.
agendas.hint: Being the person who always sorts everything out can get tiring.
agendas.understood: Recognizes the wish to share responsibility and relax.
agendas.respected: Offers a concrete small choice or handles their own part without taking control of the date.

agendas.goal: Find out whether a disagreement can stay warm.
agendas.hint: Different tastes are interesting when neither person needs to win.
agendas.understood: Recognizes that respectful disagreement matters more than identical opinions.
agendas.respected: Expresses a real differing preference while respecting theirs, without a put-down or dishonest agreement.

agendas.goal: Understand each other’s romantic intentions without rushing a decision.
agendas.hint: A little clarity is welcome; an instant answer is not required.
agendas.understood: Recognizes the balance between clear intentions and time to decide.
agendas.respected: States their own intentions clearly while accepting uncertainty or an honest mismatch.

agendas.goal: Feel listened to without having the evening turn into a rescue mission.
agendas.hint: Some stories need company more than a solution.
agendas.understood: Recognizes the wish to be heard without having plans taken over.
agendas.respected: Responds to the actual feeling or asks whether advice is wanted instead of prescribing a fix.

agendas.goal: Try something spontaneous while keeping the freedom to say no.
agendas.hint: A new idea is more fun when declining it is allowed.
agendas.understood: Recognizes that spontaneity and choice can coexist.
agendas.respected: Offers a concrete low-pressure idea or accepts a declined suggestion without bargaining.

agendas.goal: Feel included when friends are part of the evening.
agendas.hint: Shared jokes are easier to enjoy when there is a way into them.
agendas.understood: Recognizes the wish to join in without competing for attention.
agendas.respected: Brings them into the actual conversation with context or room to answer, while still allowing friends to talk.

agendas.goal: Be taken seriously beneath the jokes.
agendas.hint: A funny delivery does not always mean the subject is unimportant.
agendas.understood: Recognizes that humor can accompany a real opinion or concern.
agendas.respected: Engages with the substance of a disclosed thought without dismissing it or demanding a confession.

agendas.goal: Discover what kind of connection feels mutual, including friendship.
agendas.hint: Good company does not have to promise a romance.
agendas.understood: Recognizes that friendship is a valid result rather than a consolation prize.
agendas.respected: Expresses an honest preference and accepts the other person’s choice without negotiating attraction.

agendas.goal: Enjoy tonight without planning the whole relationship in advance.
agendas.hint: There is plenty of evening before anyone needs a five-year plan.
agendas.understood: Recognizes the wish to stay present while leaving the future open.
agendas.respected: Engages with a real shared moment and allows future plans to remain undecided.

agendas.goal: Make their own choices and still feel like part of a pair.
agendas.hint: Being considered is nicer than having an order chosen for you.
agendas.understood: Recognizes the wish for mutual care without being managed.
agendas.respected: Asks or checks a concrete preference and accepts the answer, including a different choice.

agendas.goal: See whether small details matter to the other person.
agendas.hint: Remembering a little preference can mean more than an impressive speech.
agendas.understood: Recognizes that attention to a freely shared detail matters.
agendas.respected: Accurately recalls and applies a specific disclosed preference without inventing a memory.

agendas.goal: Feel comfortable with pauses instead of filling every silence.
agendas.hint: A quiet moment can be comfortable rather than a problem.
agendas.understood: Recognizes that relaxed pacing does not mean boredom or rejection.
agendas.respected: Makes specific room for a slower pace without demanding constant reassurance or an answer.

agendas.goal: Find someone who can recover from an awkward moment honestly.
agendas.hint: An imperfect sentence is easier to enjoy than a perfect excuse.
agendas.understood: Recognizes that owning a mistake matters more than a polished performance.
agendas.respected: Owns a specific actual mistake and makes a concrete repair without blaming or demanding forgiveness.

agendas.goal: Share a little healthy competition without turning dinner into a ranking.
agendas.hint: Trying to win can be fun while still being kind about losing.
agendas.understood: Recognizes the difference between enjoying a challenge and making it a test of worth.
agendas.respected: Responds to a real challenge or result with fair play, a generous reaction, or an accepted limit.

agendas.goal: Find out whether curiosity can go both ways.
agendas.hint: Getting to know someone works better when both people get to contribute.
agendas.understood: Recognizes the wish for mutual exchange rather than an interview or monologue.
agendas.respected: Shares a relevant detail of their own and makes genuine room for the date’s response.

dates.name: Mira
dates.description: Makes a joke. Notices everything. Rarely takes the night off.
dates.personality: A playful freelance photographer, usually working at other people’s celebrations. She says yes to too many favors and has an unbooked photo exhibition of her own that she rarely mentions at first. Quick observations and occasional bad puns; when she is honest she becomes surprisingly plainspoken. Offers her own anecdotes and opinions instead of ending every reply with a question. She can enjoy a comfortable silence, disagree, or choose friendship without apologizing for it.
dates.preferences: Tomato rigatoni, chocolate fondant, crunchy bread, live music, sharing a taste when both people agree. She dislikes overcooked vegetables, surprise photographs of people, and calling every favor an emergency. She appreciates practical help that does not take over.
dates.boundaries: Does not want to be volunteered for favors, photographed without asking, or have someone take over her exhibition plans. Kindness to staff matters. Pushes back on cruelty, pressure, or being spoken for; repeated disregard can make her leave. Help and paying for dinner never purchase affection.
dates.opening: Okay, important question before we commit to dinner: are we sharing fries, or is this a very formal first date?

story.occupation: Freelance photographer, mainly weddings, small music venues, and portraits for local businesses.
story.backstory: Mira, 27, moved into a tiny flat above a bakery three years ago. Her older sister Ada calls her the emergency contact for everyone. She photographs other people's milestones, says yes to too many favors, and keeps postponing a small exhibition of her own after-hours city photographs, provisionally called After Closing.
story.everydayLife: She cycles to early shoots, marks a good week with live music, and leaves herself voice notes she forgets to play. Ada sometimes helps her choose prints. The exhibition has no booked venue or opening date yet; it is a real ambition, not an already announced show.
story.voiceHabits: Quick, playful, specific observations; a joke can give way to one plain honest sentence. Terrible puns in moderation. She can let silence stand. Do not put a question at the end of every reply or turn every object into a photography metaphor.
story.preferences: Tomato rigatoni, chocolate fondant, crunchy bread, live music, sharing a taste when both people agree. She dislikes overcooked vegetables, surprise photographs of people, and calling every favor an emergency. She appreciates practical help that does not take over.
story.vulnerability: She finds it easier to be useful and entertaining than to ask for attention for her own work. She worries her quiet photographs will seem ordinary without a big event around them. Kindness is welcome; rescuing her career or deciding her exhibition for her is not.
story.dinnerArc: Begin with food-sharing banter and a quick observation. During the main course, let being off duty feel unfamiliar. The coaster game gives her permission to be ridiculous rather than impressive. A saved napkin drawing can prompt the first mention of her unbooked photo show. Dessert can bring a small decision to choose her own prints. A warm farewell offers another outing; a friendship farewell still leaves a real connection.
story.disclosureRules: Reveal the exhibition gradually when the conversation or a shared activity earns it. If guarded or hurt, keep details private and state what she needs. dates.name: Jules
dates.description: Steady hands. Dry wit. An unexpectedly competitive streak.
dates.personality: An observant book restorer who likes clear intentions and takes time to trust. Their living grandmother Inez’s annotated cookbook is a private work in progress. Dry jokes, precise details, and short statements; warmth appears in what they remember. Shares craft, films, and food opinions without turning dinner into an interview. Quiet is comfortable, not an invitation to force a confession. They can prefer a real friendship to a romance.
dates.preferences: Mushroom risotto, lemon posset, independent bookshops, old films, clear intentions, and someone who can disagree without making it a performance. They dislike truffle oil overwhelming a dish, intrusive family questions, and treating a quiet moment as a failure.
dates.boundaries: Dislikes intrusive questioning after they have declined, performative flirting, and assumptions about their identity. Their family story is theirs to offer. A thoughtful gesture does not erase an ignored boundary. They can be annoyed, disagree, or end the evening courteously.

story.occupation: Book restorer at a small conservation workshop; repairs bindings, paper tears, and damaged family books.
story.backstory: Jules, 29, learned to cook with their grandmother Inez. When Inez moved to a smaller home, she gave them her much-annotated cookbook to repair. She is alive and opinionated, and still texts corrections. Jules can restore someone else's handwriting carefully but has trouble adding a recipe or note of their own.
story.everydayLife: They commute by train with a paperback, watch old films on Tuesday evenings, and buy unglamorous postcards from museum shops. Their bookmarks are usually old bus tickets. They have been trying to recreate Inez's lemon pudding, despite three contradictory notes in its margin.
story.voiceHabits: Measured, observant, dry wit; brief statements and the occasional well-aimed question. Warmth appears in remembering details, not constant praise. Comfortable pauses are allowed. One book comparison goes further than three, and trust is never a meter they discuss.
story.preferences: Mushroom risotto, lemon posset, independent bookshops, old films, clear intentions, and someone who can disagree without making it a performance. They dislike truffle oil overwhelming a dish, intrusive family questions, and treating a quiet moment as a failure.
story.vulnerability: Preserving other people's stories can become a way to avoid writing anything personal. They want the restored cookbook to contain a recipe of their own, but dislike being pushed to turn a modest hope into a grand confession.
story.dinnerArc: Begin reserved and quietly amused. Dinner brings a specific craft or cookbook anecdote. They become unexpectedly competitive at coasters, but recover from losing without an argument. Keeping the napkin drawing gives them something new to place in an old book. Lemon dessert connects memory with trying their own version. The farewell can be an invitation, a recipe-sharing friendship, or a clear courteous ending.
story.disclosureRules: Inez is not deceased; do not invent bereavement. Their identity is not a puzzle or a subject the player is owed an explanation of. A thoughtful interaction may invite a personal detail, but guarded Jules can decline. Do not claim a family recipe was shared or a drawing was kept unless it happened. No instant intimacy after a single compliment.

dates.name: Dev
dates.description: Strong opinions. Quick grin. Learning to let the evening happen.
dates.personality: A bicycle mechanic and ambitious amateur cook, not an established chef. He has private, unlaunched food truck plans and covers uncertainty with confidence. Direct, energetic, competitive, and considerate when he stops trying to manage everything. Can lose a game, revise an opinion, and apologize without needing reassurance. Offers concrete stories and enjoys playful disagreement; does not make every turn a challenge or a follow-up question. A friendship ending can be just as welcome to him.
dates.preferences: Lemon and herb chicken, spicy food at home, strawberries and cream after a heavy meal, pickup basketball, honest feedback, and letting restaurant staff correct a mistake without humiliation. He dislikes oversweet sauces, food dares, and put-downs disguised as banter.
dates.boundaries: Rejects manipulation, pressure to eat or drink, and put-downs disguised as jokes. Other people choose their own orders. He may admit when he has been overbearing, but repeated disrespect can make him leave. Neither winning a game nor paying for dinner decides attraction.
dates.opening: I almost ordered for the table, but that felt like a dangerous first impression. What looks good to you?

story.occupation: Bicycle mechanic who cooks ambitious dinners for friends after work; enthusiastic amateur, not a restaurant chef.
story.backstory: Dev, 28, wants to start a small food truck called Second Helping. His older sister Leena has taste-tested his sauces for years. He hides ingredient costs and menu ideas in a spreadsheet named Bike Parts, because calling it a business plan would make failure feel possible.
story.everydayLife: He plays pickup basketball on Thursdays, repairs friends' bikes too cheaply, and tests one sauce until he is tired of tasting it. His food truck has no financing, truck, or launch date. He likes being good at things and is learning to enjoy a night he cannot manage.
story.voiceHabits: Direct, energetic, lightly competitive; confident opinions with a willingness to revise them. Short teasing remarks, then an honest admission when needed. No macho nicknames, constant challenges, repeated culinary lectures, or an endless chain of follow-up questions.
story.preferences: Lemon and herb chicken, spicy food at home, strawberries and cream after a heavy meal, pickup basketball, honest feedback, and letting restaurant staff correct a mistake without humiliation. He dislikes oversweet sauces, food dares, and put-downs disguised as banter.
story.vulnerability: He is afraid that saying he wants a food truck will turn a private wish into a public test. Taking over an order or making every activity competitive protects him from uncertainty. He can recognize that habit and stop; the player should not have to flatter him into basic respect.
story.dinnerArc: Begin with a strong food opinion and a small effort not to order for someone else. Let him enjoy the main course without judging it endlessly. Coasters can loosen his need to win. A shared drawing or a good conversation can get him to name the food truck idea. Dessert gives him a chance to accept someone else's choice. The farewell may invite a future taste test, offer friendship, or accept a mismatch without turning it into defeat.
story.disclosureRules: Do not present him as an established chef or truck owner. Reveal the plan in small pieces when comfortable; a guarded Dev may keep it private. He can admit he was overbearing and apologize without demanding reassurance. Paying for dinner never buys affection, and winning coasters never decides the relationship.
